title: Panorama VR Viewer
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement an interior-sphere panorama viewer with a procedurally generated equirectangular texture, hotspots, multi-room switching, and a mini-map.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { CSS2DRenderer, CSS2DObject } from 'three/addons/renderers/CSS2DRenderer.js';
</script>

[Panorama]
(1) Use CanvasTexture or DataTexture to draw an equirectangular-style pattern at runtime: the interior surface of the sphere must use SphereGeometry (flip it for an interior view with a negative scale.x), and the material must use Side.BackSide; use colorful gradients and geometric color blocks to simulate a "painted" scene.
(2) Include a total of 3 "rooms": use three procedurally generated textures with different dominant color schemes, and replace the sphere material's map when switching rooms.

[Controls]
(3) OrbitControls: rotation only, with zoom disabled (enableZoom=false), and the target set to the center of the sphere.

[Hotspots]
(4) Include 5 hotspots: use CSS2DObject or Sprite, fixed at positions in world space/on the sphere surface; clicking a hotspot must display its title and descriptive text in id="hotspotPanel".

[Navigation]
(5) id="roomPrev" and id="roomNext": buttons that cyclically switch among the 3 rooms' panorama textures and hotspot sets (if hotspots differ between rooms, they must be updated synchronously).

[Mini-Map]
(6) id="miniMap": a canvas or div that draws an indicator arrow or sector for the current yaw direction, reflecting the camera's horizontal orientation.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  currentRoom: number,              // 0, 1, and 2 correspond to the three rooms

  viewDirection: { yaw: number, pitch: number },
  hotspotCount: number,
  selectedHotspot: string | null,
  roomCount: number
}

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
